name: Empiricism
body:
Empirical studies are methods of investigation tried and true over many generations. These s-class investigators rely on keen deductive reasoning and insight to solve cases.

That’s Odd (Ex)

At 1st level, the investigator can find clues even in the most unlikely of places. When he enters a location for the first time, the investigator can spend 1 inspiration and discover something about his immediate area that may not have been there previously. He can do this once per day without spending inspiration at 1st level and every 3 levels thereafter (4th, 7th, and so on), up to 7 times per day at 19th level.

Examples include:

A clue to his current quest that was either dropped or placed there for him to find.
A key that fits into either the next locked door or a previously discovered locked door.
A note pleading for help, leading to a new adventure.
A hidden panel, switch, or weak point in a wall that can be blown open,opening into a previously unknown room or set of stairs.
A nearby npc is actually an enemy in disguise.

Regardless of what he discovers, the investigator cannot use this ability in the same location more than once, nor can he use it in a room discovered using that’s odd.

The gamemaster decides what is discovered when this ability is used, and while it is ultimately helpful, the discovery may be cryptic or otherwise difficult to understand immediately, such as a puzzle that must be solved to open a door, or a strange message that, when deciphered, can lead the investigator to his next location.

Ceaseless Observation (Ex)

At 2nd level, the investigator uses his Intelligence modifier instead of the skill’s typical ability for all Disable Device, Perception, Sense Motive, and Use Magic Device checks. He can also use his Intelligence modifier instead of Charisma on any Diplomacy checks made to gather information.

If the investigator also uses the brohk methodology, he applies Charisma to the skills above instead, as well as on all Linguistics and monster lore checks made with a Knowledge skill.

Empirical Eye

In addition to his normal selection of talents, the investigator gains bonus talents at 5th, 11th, and 17th level. He can choose from amazing inspiration, inspired alertness, and quick study, even if he doesn’t meet the prerequisites.

Unfailing Logic (Ex)

The investigator’s grasp of facts and data teaches him to anchor himself in reality, granting resistance to even the most potent illusions.

At 4th level, the investigator gains a +2 insight bonus on all Will saving throws against illusion spells or spell-like abilities that allow a save to disbelieve their effects. In addition he can spend one point from his inspiration pool as an immediate action to use his Intelligence bonus instead of her Wisdom bonus on all such saves for one round.

At 8th level, the empiricist’s insight bonus increases to +4.

At 16th level, he gains immunity to all illusion spells and spell-like abilities that allow a save to disbelieve the effects.

Master Intellect (Ex)

At 19th level, the investigator can use inspiration on all skills (even ones he is not trained in) and all ability checks (including initiative checks) without spending inspiration.
